answers.answer: Shuffle the three tiers separately. From top to bottom, deal 1 randomly selected card from Conflict I, then 5 randomly selected cards from Conflict II, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘three separately shuffled tiers’; ‘1 card ... Conflict I; 5 cards ... Conflict II; all 4 Conflict III’; ‘Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In either player count, each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 3 troops in their garrison (with 9 other troops in supply), 1 water, and one Influence cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction tracks. Starting VP is 0 in a three-player game and 1 in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘2 Agents on their Leader’; ‘third Agent ... Swordmaster’; ‘1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise ... 0’; ‘3 [troops] in the circular garrison’; ‘takes 1 water’; cubes on bottom spaces of four tracks.

answers.answer: Yes. You may choose a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. After taking it, your turns are skipped for the rest of the Player Turns phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn later in that phase. Plot Intrigue may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn, but not after your Reveal turn once your turns have been skipped.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: ‘Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left’; ‘Once you have taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped’; Plot cards may be played ‘during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.’

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one of its Agent icons matching the chosen board space; one card sends only one Agent. The space must be unoccupied. You must meet its requirements and pay its costs immediately, before resolving effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot send the Agent there. Then resolve the space effect, the card’s Agent box, and the one-space Influence advancement for a Faction space in any order. The card’s Reveal box is ignored on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: ‘play one card ... to an unoccupied board space’; ‘choose only one Agent icon’; ‘can't send an Agent’ to an occupied space; costs ‘paid immediately, before resolving any effects’; effects ... ‘in any order.’

answers.answer: No. Conspire requires 4 spice and costs must be paid before resolving any effect of the space or card, so an Agent card’s spice gain cannot cover the entry cost when you have only 3. After a legal placement and payment, you may resolve the board-space effect, card Agent box, and one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Conspire costs ‘4 spice’; costs are paid ‘before resolving any effects of the space or the played card’; space, Agent box, and Influence advancement may resolve ‘in any order’ after paying entry cost.

answers.answer: You recruited 3 troops total, and on this Combat-space Agent turn you may deploy any or all of those recruits plus up to 2 troops from your garrison. With 4 already garrisoned, the maximum deployment is 5 troops (all 3 recruits and 2 from the garrison). Any recruits not deployed go to your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its four recruits normally go to your garrison and cannot be deployed by that turn’s Rally Troops action.
answers.evidence: At a Combat space, deploy ‘any or all troops you recruited this turn ... plus up to two more troops from your garrison’; undeployed recruits ‘go to your garrison’; Rally Troops is ‘not a Combat space, so they go to your garrison.’

answers.answer: Reveal turn order: (1) reveal all cards remaining in your hand, keeping them separate from Agent-turn cards; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of the newly revealed cards in any order and spend Persuasion to acquire cards before, between, or after those effects; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up by putting all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile. Only cards revealed during this Reveal turn use their Reveal boxes.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn lists four ordered steps: ‘Reveal Cards,’ ‘Resolve Reveal Effects,’ ‘Set Strength,’ ‘Clean Up’; step 2 specifies boxes of cards ‘you just revealed,’ and cleanup says all cards from Agent and Reveal turns go to discard.

answers.answer: Yes, after acquiring a Row card the Row refills immediately, so you may buy its replacement if you can afford it. Persuasion can be pooled across sources for one card or split across cards; unused Persuasion is lost and cannot be saved. Acquired cards go to your discard pile and are not used immediately. An Acquire-box effect happens once at the moment the card is acquired.
answers.evidence: The Imperium Row refills ‘immediately ... so after acquiring a card you may also acquire its replacement’; Persuasion ‘can never be saved’; acquired cards go to discard and ‘you don't use them right away’; Acquire effect happens ‘at the moment you acquire the card.’

answers.answer: Strength is 10: 3 troops in the Conflict contribute 6 and 4 revealed swords contribute 4. If your last deployed troop is removed, your strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by swords or any other means. For strength over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop is worth ‘2 strength’ and each revealed sword ‘1 strength’; without a troop strength is 0 ‘including swords’; over 20, flip to ‘+20’ and start at the beginning.

answers.answer: During Combat, starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing earlier does not bind a player to pass again; Combat resolves after all involved players pass consecutively. ‘When you win’ Intrigue cards are played only after winning, before the next phase (and a first-place tie has no winner).
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: order begins ‘with the First Player’; eligible players have ‘at least one troop’; ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after consecutive passes; win-trigger cards ‘only after you've won, before moving to the next phase.’

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins and each takes the second reward. C and D then compete for the third reward; since C beats D, C takes it and D gets nothing. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, even in two- or three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength receives no reward. After rewards, each player returns Conflict troops to their supply, not their garrison.
answers.evidence: First-place tie: ‘each tied player receives the second reward’ and in a 4-player game ‘the other two still compete for the third reward’; second-place ties get third reward each; third-place ties get nothing; 0 strength gets no reward; troops return to supply.

answers.answer: Normal harvesting happens when an Agent resolves the effect of a Maker space during Player Turns. In Phase 4: Makers, after Combat, add 1 bonus spice from the bank to each empty Maker space: The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; accumulated bonus spice remains there. If an Agent moves away and the Maker space is empty in Phase 4, it still receives the bonus. A later Agent visit gains the space’s normal spice plus any accumulated bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Phase order places ‘Makers’ after Combat; each empty Great Flat, Hagga Basin, or Imperial Basin gets 1 spice, adding to accumulated bonus; ruling says if an Agent moves away and it is still empty in Phase 4, bonus spice accumulates. Space effects give listed base spice ‘plus any bonus spice.’

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately; at Phase 5: Recall, the game ends at the end of a round if a player has 10 or more VP. The game also ends at that checkpoint if the Conflict Deck is empty after the last Conflict was revealed and played. Before deciding the winner, players resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards. The tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops (not troops in supply), then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Game-end trigger is ‘at the end of a round (Phase 5: Recall)’ with 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck; ‘first, players may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards’; tiebreaks list spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, you gain 1 VP; dropping below 2 loses that VP, and returning to 2 regains it. At 4 Influence, you receive the track bonus; you keep it if you later fall below 4 and can earn it again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP. Tying the holder does not take it, but advancing to a higher Influence space does. If the holder loses Influence while previously tied, a previously tied player takes the token; with several tied players, the former holder chooses one.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: VP at 2 is ‘lost if you drop below 2, regained if you reach 2 again’; 4-Influence bonus ‘do not give ... back’ and can be earned again; Alliance transfers only when passed by rising ‘to a higher space’; prior tied player takes it if holder loses Influence.

answers.answer: At 5 Influence, if you lose 1 and drop to 4 while two opponents remain tied with you at 5, the Alliance transfers to one of those previously tied opponents; because there are several tied, you choose which one. If instead you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, no player has 4 or more to take it, so the token returns to the board and you lose its VP.
answers.evidence: If holder loses Influence while previously tied, ‘the previously tied player takes it; if several were tied, the holder chooses one.’ Holder also loses it at 3 or less; if no player has 4 or more, ‘return it to the board.’

answers.answer: Discarding means taking a card from your hand unless otherwise specified and putting it in your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle an empty deck early just to inspect its top card; reshuffle the discard pile only when unable to draw because the deck is empty.
answers.evidence: ‘Discard’ means a card from hand ... to discard pile; trashing can remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play; Reserve cards return to Reserve; trashing optional unless cost/self-trash; cannot reshuffle early to inspect an empty deck.

answers.answer: Control bonuses pay whenever any player, including the controller, sends an Agent to the controlled location: Arrakeen and Carthag pay 1 Solari; Imperial Basin pays 1 spice. Winning a Conflict titled for one of those locations lets you place your Control marker there, replacing an opponent’s marker. Later, when a Conflict for a location you already control is revealed, you may deploy 1 troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning a matching Conflict places a marker ‘replacing any opponent's marker’; while there, bonus applies whenever ‘any player’ visits; when matching Conflict is revealed, may deploy ‘one troop from your supply.’

answers.answer: For setup, choose an unused color, put one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks, and put remaining cubes in its supply; it has no troops in its garrison. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards, and place that deck and its three Agents near its supply. Use no Rival Leader or solo difficulty rules. After each First Player Agent turn, it takes an Agent turn if it has an Agent left, up to three Rival turns per round; it does not act after the other human’s turn or a Reveal turn and never Reveals. It collects no resources, builds no Imperium deck, earns no Conflict rewards or VP, and cannot claim Control; it can take and hold Faction Alliances.
answers.evidence: House Hagal setup specifies unused color, one cube on each track, no troops in garrison, remove three 1P Arrakeen cards, remaining deck and ‘three Agents’; turns follow each First Player Agent turn; it ‘never takes a Reveal turn’; no resources/rewards/VP/Control but can hold Alliances.

answers.answer: If the indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. If the House Hagal deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, reshuffle immediately and continue. Ignore normal space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the card’s icons and instructions. A troop icon recruits a troop, deployed if the destination is a Combat space and otherwise placed in its garrison. Whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, it automatically deploys 2 garrison troops if available, 1 if only one is available, or none if empty. Harvest Spice follows its card instructions, but harvested bonus spice is removed from the space and returned to the bank. For a two-space card, use only the option matching current conditions; if that option is occupied, draw another card rather than switching to the other option.
answers.evidence: Occupied-space procedure says keep revealing; reshuffle if deck empty or Reshuffle appears; ignore space costs/requirements/effects; troop icons recruit and deploy only at Combat spaces; automatically deploy up to two garrison troops; harvested bonus spice returns to bank; two-space cards never switch options if the applicable one is occupied.

answers.answer: If House Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, at the start of Combat reveal a House Hagal card; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Add the revealed card’s sword icons to its normal 2 strength per deployed troop. Hagal receives no reward for its rank but occupies that rank when humans receive rewards. If it wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove the human’s Control marker and do not replace it with Hagal’s. A human tie for second receives the third reward for each tied player, even though ordinary third place is unavailable in a two-player game.
answers.evidence: Hagal strength: reveal at Combat start, reshuffle and reveal again if Reshuffle; add sword icons to ‘2 strength per deployed troop’; it gets no rank reward but occupies rank; if it wins a human-controlled space, remove marker; human second-place ties get third reward even in two-player games.
